request: what does the dot product measure?

beats.intent: A plane with v = (3, 1) and w = (2, 2)
beats.narration: Take two vectors, v is three, one and w is two, two.
beats.code:
stage.title("The dot product")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (3, 1), color=YELLOW, label="v")
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 2), color=BLUE, label="w")

beats.intent: The shadow of v dropped onto w's line
beats.narration: Drop v's shadow onto the line of w. The dot product is the shadow's length times the length of w.
In numbers: multiply matching parts and add. Three times two plus one times two is eight.

beats.intent: Perpendicular vectors (1, 2) and (2, -1) with a right-angle mark, dot product 0
beats.narration: Now turn them to a right angle: one, two and two, minus one. The shadow shrinks to a point, and the dot product is zero.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
p2 = draw_plane(stage)
a = draw_vector(stage, p2, (1, 2), color=YELLOW, label="a")
b = draw_vector(stage, p2, (2, -1), color=BLUE, label="b")
sq = RightAngle(Line(p2.c2p(0, 0), p2.c2p(1, 2)), Line(p2.c2p(0, 0), p2.c2p(2, -1)), length=0.3, quadrant=(1, 1), color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(sq))
stage.add(sq)
stage.equation(r"1 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot (-1) = 0")

beats.intent: A grid with a yellow arrow on the x-axis and a green arrow along (1, -1)
beats.narration: Here is a grid. Watch what the matrix three, one, zero, two does to it.

beats.intent: The grid transformed: the arrows on (1, 0) and (1, -1) stay on their lines, another arrow is knocked off
beats.narration: Most arrows get knocked off their line. But arrows along one, zero and along one, minus one only stretch.

beats.intent: The picture beside A(1, 0) = 3(1, 0) and A(1, -1) = 2(1, -1)
beats.narration: The first is stretched by three, the second by two. Those stretch factors are the eigenvalues.

request: how can the same point have different coordinates?

beats.intent: A plane with the point (2, 0) and its arrow
beats.narration: On the usual grid, this arrow ends at two, zero.
beats.code:
stage.title("Changing the basis")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 0), color=YELLOW, label="(2, 0)")

beats.intent: A tilted grid built from b1 = (1, 1) and b2 = (-1, 1) over the plane
beats.narration: Now build a new grid from two other arrows: one, one and minus one, one.
beats.code:
b1 = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 1), color=GREEN, label="b_1")
b2 = draw_vector(stage, p, (-1, 1), color=RED, label="b_2")
basis_grid(stage, p, (1, 1), (-1, 1))

beats.intent: The steps b1 then minus b2 reaching the same point, beside (2, 0) = 1·b1 - 1·b2
beats.narration: To reach the same point on the new grid: one step of b one, then one step back along b two. Its new coordinates are one, minus one.
beats.code:
s1 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(0, 0), p.c2p(1, 1), color=GREEN)
s2 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(1, 1), p.c2p(2, 0), color=RED)
stage.equation(r"(2, 0) = 1\,b_1 - 1\,b_2")

request: what is the span of a vector?

beats.code:
stage.title("Span")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 1), color=YELLOW, label="v")

beats.intent: The vector stretched to twice its length then flipped to minus one times
beats.narration: Scale it: twice as long, or flipped backwards. Every scaling stays on one line.
beats.code:
scale_vector(stage, p, v, 2)
scale_vector(stage, p, v, -0.5)

beats.intent: The whole line through the origin along (2, 1) lit as its span
beats.narration: All its multiples together fill that line. The line is the span of v.
beats.code:
draw_span(stage, p, (2, 1))
stage.caption("span of one vector: a line")

beats.intent: A second vector (-1, 2) added and the caption: two vectors span the whole plane
beats.narration: Add a second vector that points another way. Mixing the two reaches every point: the span is the whole plane.
beats.code:
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (-1, 2), color=GREEN, label="w")
draw_span(stage, p, (-1, 2), color=GREEN)
stage.caption("two independent vectors: the whole plane")
